recipes.name: Ethiopian Cabbage Dish
ingredients_raw: 5 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add carrots and onion; cook and stir until beginning to soften, about 5 minutes. Stir in cabbage, salt, pepper, cumin, and turmeric; cook for 15 to 20 minutes.
Add potatoes; reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook until potatoes are soft, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Ethiopian Cabbage Dish
raw_recipe.description: Green cabbage and potatoes are paired with tender vegetables and warming spices in this Ethiopian side dish that's perfect for weeknight dinners.

review.reviewBody: Ethiopian is probably my favorite kind of food, but I'd never tried making any real dishes (I live in the DC area where Ethio restaurants are all over). The restaurants call this dish tikil gomen. I have to say this tasted almost exactly like the tikil gomen I've had before--this is probably partially because I doubled the spices (as recommended) and also used niter kibbeh, Ethiopian spiced clarified butter, instead of olive oil. (There are many various recipes for niter kibbeh online--it's really flavorful and keeps for months!) I was just looking for something to make with cabbage and potatoes, but I'm glad I found this because it inspired me to make an Ethiopian dinner with Ethiopian lentils (mesir wat). This dish turned out much better than the lentils! Definitely a keeper!

first i sauteed a single costco pack of boneless skinless thighs, put that aside, dropped in a diced small half of an onion, sauteed that pulled that to the side, added a half of a cabbage, chopped, sauteed that for a minute while i chopped a pre-baked potato, dropped that plus the chicken and onion in, added the spices and stirred gently and then put a lid on the pan and steamed for about 3 minutes. bonus add warm hummus and a costco naan or 2 and some harrissa, bam

I ABSOLUTELY LOVE THIS, but I did make some changes. Since I don't like mushy veggies, I would never cook cabbage for 40 min. I pan fried the potatoes 1st (skin on) to add a contrasting texture - crunchy outside, soft inside. I also stir fried the cabbage along with the other ingredients and added mushrooms because why not?? It was DELISH!

This is so flavorful! We just loved it. I doubled the spices as several suggested. I used about 1/3 C. Oil. I added small chicken pieces because I wanted this as the main meal. I tossed all ingredients until everything was evenly coated with oil and spices. I put them in my air fryer and cooked at 400 degrees for 13 minutes. I liked the little bit of crisp.

Simplicity, it’s about a new technique; using cumin seed and grinding in a pestle will make the prescribed amount of spice sufficient. When folk ‘make it their own’ they typically miss the subtle simplicity of the ingredients… it’s cabbage and potato playing off of the aromatic’s. I highly recommend trying this recipe over again and do not forget sea salt (salt releases liquid from vegetables) and always use freshly ground cumin due to its exquisite volatility.

Very tasty; even hubby liked it. Used brussel sprouts cut in half instead of cabbage (as that is what I had), and doubled the spices as everyone said. Added brussel sprouts and potatoes when I added the carrots and onions. Used 1/4 cup of avocado oil, on low heat and added 1/4 cup water about half way through; cooked total of 45 minutes until everything was well steamed. Very tasty. Will definitely make again.

Love it! I took a page from another comment and added apple cider vinegar to the recipe. I used less oil. Also, I added to potatoes at the same time as the onions and carrots. I didn’t want the cabbage to be over cooked. I also cooked in a wok. It was great!

This is a great quick and easy meal. I season to taste which was more than listed in the recipe. I also like my potatoes with a little crispness to them and I don’t like my cabbage super soft, so I cooked the potatoes separate from the cabbage and combined at the end.

This is great the next morning with a fried egg on top! 

I added the potatoes and cabbage at the same time, which needed about 30 min. to cook. I halved the oil to 1/4 cup, but added a few splashes of veggie broth after 20 min. as it was starting to stick. 

I used multi-color baby potatoes with the skin on, quartered, which made it pretty (and easier not to peel). Also added some minced jalapeno as another reviewer suggested, but couldn't really taste it so next time I'll add more! A tasty, healthy, simple dish.

I really enjoyed this combination of spices. I've made many cabbage hashes before, but not with these spices and never with potatoes. I loved the addition of both. I didn't follow the recipe to the letter, I didn't see the need for so much oil. I used perhaps 2 tablespoons of EVOO, and maybe a 1/3 cup of chicken broth to add moistness and omitted the salt. I added in some kielbasa to make a more complete meal and, therefore, didn't add any additional salt. I'll use this recipe again.

The smell of this cooking is simply mouth-watering. After reading all the comments, I opted to add the potatoes right after the carrots, onion, and three cloves of garlic I added. Then, a few minutes later, added the cabbage. I like spicy stuff, so I doubled the spices as did most others, and used only about half of the oil it called for. To keep it from getting dry I added a bit of water a couple of times. This dish is outstanding. I would have eaten it vegetarian as written, but I have housemates who wouldn't have enjoyed that, so I added some Kielbasa at the end. I struggle with rating things if I make changes, but....I wanted to be honest about what I did and the only big change was adding the sausage to make this a main dish for dinner. I will most definitely make this again and again!
Did double the spices plus a pinch of red pepper, added a can of white beans for protein and served it over quinoa.

I listened to the tweakers and made some tweaks too. I tripled the cumin and turmeric but I like spicy. I didn't have meat but I had Punjabi wadi which are like crumbly bisquets full of flavor made of lentils. I also added more oil cuz I used a whole cabbage so I didn't want it to dry out. Im glad I got introduced to Etheopian cooking

I made as suggested the first time. It was delicious. I’ve made it several times since with a few shortcuts. Partially microwaving the carrots and potatoes first and added some garlic. My next venture is to add some cherry tomatoes because I love the cooked. lol and they go well with cabbage, but then it’s a different recipe. So based on how this came out it is a keeper. Great as a main dish for vegetarians with some tofu sautéed withe the onion👍🏻👍🏻
I love it and I made no changes to the recipe
A great recipe! Loved the flavour with the spices. I will definitely this recipe again!
Be sure to boil those potatoes before adding them to the pot, then, add the cabbage at the same time. My cabbage still has a little bite left.
I love this recipe. A very nice surprise. And you add some many things chicken, sausages etc, creating many combination. I added also smoked paprika!!
So simple but tastes so good!
Easy to follow and great flavors.
